_meta.source: MOE CCA and LEAPS 2.0 guidance, polytechnic EAE and DSA-Sec published criteria, and school ECG practice
_meta.units: week is sessions a week, a plain estimate, not a measurement
_meta.notes:
What a student carries besides their subjects. Two jobs. It makes the game honest about time, which is the one thing a fourteen year old cannot buy more of, and it tells a student what the thing they already do is building and where it can go, which is the conversation an ECG counsellor would have and almost nothing on a screen ever does.

Three rules on the writing, and they are not stylistic. This file must never tell a student they are doing too much. It must never ask whether they are sure. It must never describe a commitment as a cost with nothing on the other side of it. A student carrying four evenings a week is usually carrying them for a reason, sometimes a reason nobody chose, and the last thing they need from a school website is a raised eyebrow. `work` is the next thing that would make it count, never a deficiency. `manage` is what people who carry this well actually do. `opens` is true and specific or it is not written.

`week` is an honest session count and drives the points a Journey turn has to spend. It cannot be the whole story, or the game would punish the busiest students, so the engine also pays every year for what is carried: see activityYield in engine/journey.js and the monotonicity check that holds it to that. Adding an activity can never leave a run with less to accumulate than it had.

Caring at home is in this list on purpose. It is a real commitment held by real students, it is invisible to every school system, and leaving it out would say it does not count.

activities.label: A sport CCA
activities.opens: Selectors and teachers write about people they have watched for years. Two seasons in the same sport is the kind of record a DSA or an EAE interview can actually read.
activities.work: Learn to say what you do well in words. Interviews ask, and training does not teach it.
activities.manage: Training nights are gone before the week starts. Put the heavy homework on the nights that are not.

activities.label: A uniformed group
activities.opens: Ranks and badges are a written record of responsibility you were given young. Very few sixteen year olds have one.
activities.work: Notice what you are actually good at in there. Most people can only name the badge.
activities.manage: Camps eat whole weekends. Look at the term calendar early and move the deadlines you can.

activities.label: A performing arts CCA
activities.opens: Every performance is portfolio material. Arts institutions and DSA look at a body of work, and a body of work is what four years of this quietly becomes.
activities.work: Keep something from each performance. A photo, a programme, a recording. Nobody does this and everybody wishes they had.
activities.manage: Performance weeks are not normal weeks. Get ahead of them rather than through them.

activities.label: A club or society
activities.opens: Robotics, infocomm, media, debate. These are the closest thing school has to the work itself, and poly and ITE lecturers recognise them on sight.
activities.work: Build one thing all the way to finished. One finished thing beats five started ones.
activities.manage: This one is easy to let slide because nobody chases you. Give it a fixed slot.

activities.label: Student leadership
activities.opens: Prefect, class committee, council. You end up known by teachers who write testimonials, and known is the whole point of a referee.
activities.work: Take one job that is genuinely yours, not a title. Titles read thin.
activities.manage: Meetings appear at short notice. Keep one evening a week clear on purpose.

activities.label: Service to other people
activities.opens: Going back to the same place matters more than the hours. Health and social service courses ask what you kept doing, not what you tried once.
activities.work: Stay with one group long enough that they know your name.
activities.manage: Fix it to a date, not a mood. Once a month that actually happens beats every week that does not.

activities.label: Training for a competition
activities.opens: Olympiad, hackathon, national schools. A result is worth something and the preparation is worth more, because you learn how you work when it is hard.
activities.work: Write down what you tried after each round. That record is the thing you will still have in three years.
activities.manage: The weeks before are heavy and the weeks after are empty. Use the empty ones.

activities.label: Training with a club outside school
activities.opens: Coaches outside school see a different version of you, and they can say things a teacher cannot. A referee who has watched you for three years is rare.
activities.work: Ask your coach what the next level actually asks for. They know and they are waiting to be asked.
activities.manage: Travel time is real time. Count it, and stop pretending the evening is longer than it is.

activities.label: Something you make on your own
activities.opens: Music, art, code, writing, video. Portfolio routes into design, media and computing care about what you made, and nobody asks which CCA it came from.
activities.work: Put it somewhere it can be seen. Work nobody can find does not count as work you did.
activities.manage: This is the one that gets dropped first in an exam term. Keep a small version going instead of stopping.

activities.label: A weekly community group
activities.opens: You know adults outside your family and your school. That is a wider set of people to ask than most of your class has.
activities.work: Say out loud, once, what you are thinking about doing after school. Somebody there will know somebody.
activities.manage: It is on the same day every week, which makes it the easiest thing in your week to plan around.

activities.label: Looking after people at home
activities.opens: You are already doing what most people are taught in their twenties: running a day that will not wait. Health and social service courses take this seriously when you name it.
activities.work: Tell one teacher what your evenings look like. They cannot work around what they do not know.
activities.manage: The hour that is genuinely yours is usually early, not late. Find it and defend it.

activities.label: Helping with work or a family business
activities.opens: Customers, stock, money, complaints. Business and service courses teach this, and you have seen it. Say so, in those words.
activities.work: Name the parts you are trusted with. It is more than you think, and it is the part that transfers.
activities.manage: Busy periods are predictable. Ask now which weeks they are and plan school around them.

activities.label: Extra classes outside school
activities.opens: It buys back a subject you had written off, and a subject you get back is a set of courses you get back with it.
activities.work: Bring your own question. A session where you asked something is worth three where you sat.
activities.manage: It is time on top of homework, not instead of it. Decide which night the homework moves to.

copy.head: What else you carry
copy.hint: Tap what you do. Tap again to take it off.
copy.sheetNote: Nothing here is graded and nothing is compared. This is so the rest of the app can be honest about your week.
copy.empty: Nothing here yet. Add what you already do, and this says what it is building and where it can go.
copy.loadLight: About {n} a week outside lessons. There is room in your week if you want to put something in it.
copy.loadSteady: About {n} a week outside lessons. That is a real commitment, and it is the kind that leaves a record.
copy.loadFull: About {n} a week outside lessons. People who carry a week like this get good at deciding in advance what each evening is for, and that is a skill on its own.
copy.note: More is not better here and less is not worse. This is what you already carry, not a target.
copy.yearNote: Your Journey turns know about this. A fuller week has fewer spare hours in it, and what you carry pays into every year whether you spend a turn on it or not.
